quests.instruction: You feel warm, so a grown-up lays a hand across the top of your face, just below your hair. Which part are they touching?
quests.hint: It is the flat part above your eyes.
quests.explanation: The forehead is the flat part of your face between your hairline and your eyebrows. It is a handy spot for a grown-up to feel if you are warm.
quests.funFact: When you raise your eyebrows in surprise, the skin on your forehead folds into wrinkles.

quests.instruction: You puff out air to blow up a balloon. Which soft, round parts on each side of your face bulge out?
quests.hint: Smiling lifts them up.
quests.explanation: Cheeks are the soft, rounded parts on each side of your face, below your eyes. They stretch outward when you fill your mouth with air.
quests.funFact: Some people have dimples, small dents that appear in their cheeks when they smile.

quests.instruction: Which part of your face sits at the very bottom, just below your mouth?
quests.hint: On some grown-ups, a beard grows here.
quests.explanation: The chin is the lowest part of the face, under the mouth. It is the front tip of your lower jaw.
quests.funFact: Your lower jaw is the only bone in your skull that you can move on purpose.

quests.instruction: Which curved lines of hair sit just above your eyes and help keep sweat and raindrops from running into them?
quests.hint: You can raise or lower them to show how you feel.
quests.explanation: Eyebrows sit above your eyes. Their hairs slant outward, which steers drips toward the sides of your face instead of into your eyes.
quests.funFact: Raising, lowering, and wiggling your eyebrows is a big way people show feelings without saying a word.

quests.instruction: Which tiny hairs along the edge of your eyelids catch dust before it reaches your eye?
quests.hint: If something brushes against them, you blink without thinking.
quests.explanation: Eyelashes form a small fringe that traps dust and warns your eye of danger by making you blink.
quests.funFact: Eyelashes fall out and grow back every few months.

quests.instruction: To say "mmm," you press which two soft parts at the edge of your mouth together?
quests.hint: They are the colorful edges you pucker for a whistle.
quests.explanation: Lips close your mouth, keep food in while you chew, and help shape sounds like "mmm," "puh," and "buh."
quests.funFact: Your lips are packed with nerve endings, so they are among the most sensitive parts of your body.

quests.instruction: Which joint connects your hand to your arm and bends when you wave goodbye?
quests.hint: You can feel it move when you rotate your hand in a circle.
quests.explanation: The wrist lets your hand bend up, down, and side to side.
quests.funFact: Each wrist is built from eight small bones.

quests.instruction: Hold your hand out as if you are catching raindrops. Which flat, inside part of your hand faces the sky?
quests.hint: It is the broad middle of your hand, between your wrist and your fingers.
quests.explanation: Your palm is the flat part on the inside of your hand. Your fingers and thumb grow out from it.
quests.funFact: The ridges on your palms and fingertips help you grip, a bit like the tread on a shoe.

quests.instruction: Which part of your hand can swing across to touch the tip of each of your other fingers?
quests.hint: It sits apart from the rest and is shorter and wider.
quests.explanation: The thumb moves in a different direction from your fingers, so it can pinch against them to grip things.
quests.funFact: Chimpanzees and gorillas have thumbs that pinch much like yours.

quests.instruction: Find the two bony bumps on either side of your leg, just above your foot. Which joint are they part of?
quests.hint: It lets your foot point up and down.
quests.explanation: The ankle joins your lower leg to your foot. The bumps on its sides are the ends of your leg bones.
quests.funFact: The strong cord at the back of your ankle is the Achilles tendon, the thickest tendon in the body.

quests.instruction: Which part at the back of your foot usually touches the ground first when you take a step?
quests.hint: It is the rounded, padded part at the back of your foot.
quests.explanation: The heel lands first as you walk, and then your foot rolls forward onto your toes.
quests.funFact: The heel bone is the largest bone in the foot.

quests.instruction: Which joints connect the tops of your legs to your body and let you swing a leg forward and back?
quests.hint: You can feel their bony bumps when you rest your hands on your sides.
quests.explanation: The hips are the joints where your legs meet your body. They let your legs swing forward, back, and out to the sides.
quests.funFact: Your hip bones are part of the pelvis, a bowl-shaped ring of bones that supports your upper body.

quests.instruction: You lift a glass of water to your mouth. Which joint bends to bring it up?
quests.hint: It is the same joint you bend to show off a muscle.
quests.explanation: The elbow works like a hinge. It bends and straightens so you can raise things toward your face.
quests.funFact: Your elbow also helps your forearm turn, so your palm can face up or down.

quests.instruction: You climb a staircase. Which joints in your legs bend to lift each foot up to the next step?
quests.hint: They bend a lot when you walk uphill.
quests.explanation: Knees bend to lift your foot and straighten to push you up, step after step.
quests.funFact: Climbing stairs puts more pressure on your knees than walking on flat ground.

quests.instruction: You throw a ball over your head. Which joint swings your whole arm around in a big circle?
quests.hint: It is where your arm joins your body.
quests.explanation: The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint, so your arm can swing forward, back, up, and around in circles.
quests.funFact: Your shoulder blades sit on your back and glide along as you move your arm.

quests.instruction: Which thin folds of skin slide down over your eyes every time you blink?
quests.hint: They close all the way when you fall asleep.
quests.explanation: Eyelids sweep across your eyes to spread moisture and wipe away tiny specks.
quests.funFact: A single blink takes only about a tenth of a second.

quests.instruction: Which two openings at the bottom of your nose let air in and out?
quests.hint: They sit right above your upper lip.
quests.explanation: Air travels in and out through your nostrils, and smells float in along with it.
quests.funFact: A quick sniff carries extra air up to the smell sensors high inside your nose.

quests.instruction: Gently pressing two fingers on the inside of which part near your hand lets you feel your pulse?
quests.hint: Count the beats you feel and you are counting your heartbeat.
quests.explanation: Your pulse is the push of blood from each heartbeat. You can feel it clearly at your wrist because blood vessels run close to the skin there.
quests.funFact: A resting child's heart beats roughly 70 to 110 times every minute.

quests.instruction: You hold a pencil to write. Which part of your hand pinches the pencil against your fingers?
quests.hint: It is the short, wide one that sticks out to the side.
quests.explanation: Your thumb works against your fingers like one side of a pair of tongs, so you can grip a pencil.
quests.funFact: Your thumb has its own set of strong muscles, which is a big reason your grip is so powerful.

quests.instruction: You walk barefoot on warm sand. Which parts of your feet touch the sand?
quests.hint: They are the bottoms of your feet.
quests.explanation: The soles are the bottoms of your feet. Their thick skin protects you as you walk.
quests.funFact: The skin on your soles is the thickest skin on your body.

quests.instruction: The brim of a baseball cap shades which part of your face from the sun?
quests.hint: It sits just above your eyes.
quests.explanation: A brim sticks out over your forehead and shades it from the sun, along with your eyes.
quests.funFact: Skin on your forehead can sunburn as easily as skin anywhere else, so hats and sunscreen help.

quests.instruction: Your hand has a palm. Which part of your foot is the matching flat part underneath?
quests.hint: Think of the part you press against the floor.
quests.explanation: The sole is to your foot what the palm is to your hand: the flat underside.
quests.funFact: Soles have lots of nerve endings, which is why tickling your feet makes you giggle.

quests.instruction: Your arm bends at the elbow. Which joint in your leg bends in the matching way?
quests.hint: It bends the way your arm does at the elbow.
quests.explanation: Elbows and knees are both hinge joints. Each one sits in the middle of a limb and bends one way.
quests.funFact: The knee is the largest joint in your body.

quests.instruction: Your shoulder lets your arm swing in a big circle. Which joint lets your leg swing in a similar way?
quests.hint: It sits at the top of your leg.
quests.explanation: Shoulders and hips are both ball-and-socket joints, which can move in many directions.
quests.funFact: The socket of your hip is deeper than the one in your shoulder, which makes your hip steadier.

quests.instruction: A belt goes around which narrow part in the middle of your body?
quests.hint: It is between your chest and your hips.
quests.explanation: The waist is the narrow area between your chest and your hips, where belts and waistbands sit.
quests.funFact: Your waist bends and twists thanks to your spine and the strong muscles of your tummy and back.

quests.instruction: A bike helmet has a strap that buckles snugly under which part of your face?
quests.hint: It is the lowest part of your face.
quests.explanation: The chin strap keeps the helmet from sliding off, so your head stays protected if you fall.
quests.funFact: A helmet should sit level on your head, about two fingers' width above your eyebrows.

quests.instruction: In cold, dry weather, which part of your mouth often gets dry and chapped?
quests.hint: They are the soft edges around your mouth.
quests.explanation: Lips have thin skin and no oil glands of their own, so they dry out easily. Lip balm helps keep them soft.
quests.funFact: Licking your lips makes them even drier, because the moisture evaporates quickly.

quests.instruction: Palms, thumb, or soles: which one does not belong to the hand?
quests.hint: One of them belongs to your foot.
quests.explanation: Palms and thumbs are on your hand. Soles are the bottoms of your feet.
quests.funFact: Your hands and feet together hold more than half of the bones in your body.

quests.instruction: Start at the top of your leg and go down toward your foot. Which joint do you reach first?
quests.hint: It is where your leg meets your body.
quests.explanation: From top to bottom, the three joints of your leg are the hip, the knee, and the ankle.
quests.funFact: Together, your hips, knees, and ankles act like a set of hinges that soak up the bump of each step.

quests.instruction: A ballerina points her foot down like an arrow. Which joint bends to do that?
quests.hint: It is just above your foot.
quests.explanation: The ankle bends your foot up and down, which lets you point and flex.
quests.funFact: Ankles twist easily, so supportive shoes help protect them when you run and jump.
